scope: Visual audit of the existing official Vassar-frontage photograph against the local source-mesh patch renders. No additional photos were downloaded: the network download approval call was interrupted. No mesh or game assets were edited by this audit.

existingViewedPhoto.description: Vassar frontage with nearer Gates-end brick tower at image left, silver folded forms, silver curved intermediate volumes, farther Dreyfoos-end brick tower, and blue-edged canopy at image right.
existingViewedPhoto.rights: Existing photo used as an architectural reference; no public-domain or redistributable license was established.

primarySourcesRead.fact: Gates entrance is at the Main Street end; Dreyfoos entrance is at the Massachusetts Avenue end. This confirms the names independently of visual interpretation.
Credits the photo to Charles Mayer Photography. Describes steel, brick, aluminum, corrugated metal, and brightly painted red, yellow, and blue volumes, and an amphitheater facing Hockfield Court.
MIT Facilities project page credits its four-photo gallery to Andy Ryan. The gallery URLs below were discovered but not downloaded or visually audited.

coordinates.source: Blender X east, Y north, Z up; patch numbers and coordinates refer to assets-source/mit-stata/patches.json.
coordinates.names: Gates is the northeast/Main Street end; Dreyfoos is the southwest/Massachusetts Avenue end.

materials.reason: Matches the large near brick wall at the left of the official photo and the northeast source render.
Return wall of the same Gates-end brick tower; visible behind the silver folded projection.
Large Dreyfoos-end Vassar tower wall and its northeast return correspond to the farther rectangular brick volume in the official photo.
The tall straight wall southwest of the Gates folded silver cluster corresponds to the narrow high brick strip visible at the cluster's right.
Narrow return associated with patch 9; photograph does not resolve its full width clearly.
Folded vertical facets at the center of the Gates-end sculptural cluster; photo shows pale silver panels and strongly projecting rectangular window frames.

Their lower projecting prism appears to correspond to the broad silver volume in front of the Gates brick tower; source simplifies the built slopes, so this association is less certain than the large brick walls.

materials.reason: Side/rear-facing source walls are not adequately visible. Do not describe their brick/silver assignment as photographically verified.

gates.photoLandmark: Two large folded silver canopy plates below the silver facet cluster; no blue accent on these near canopies.
gates.constraint: This patch is in the correct canopy zone. Projecting its center down to terrain is a provisional implementation choice, not a photo-verified door center. The exact glazing plane beneath the canopy may be recessed or adjacent to this canopy side wall. No evidence justifies a precise numeric shift within the zone.

dreyfoos.photoLandmark: Blue-edged folded canopy at image right, at the southwest edge of the far brick tower and beside a tall narrow glazed slot.
dreyfoos.constraint: Patch 132 is a more plausible canopy/entry zone than patch 17: it is southwest of the main brick Vassar wall, near glazed-slot patch 23. Exact door center and opening normal remain unverified.

rejectedEarlierConfirmation.reason: This lies northeast of the Dreyfoos brick wall, towards the intervening round silver volumes; the blue-edged canopy in the photo lies on the opposite southwest side. An earlier verbal confirmation of patch 17 was too strong and is withdrawn.

modelingConstraints: Preserve the source massing and unequal tower offsets. The photograph combines a few large brick planes with concentrated silver folds and curved intermediate volumes; do not apply one uniform material across both towers.

Brick is warm red-orange with relatively subtle mortar. Brick tower openings are tall narrow paired-pane rectangles, usually recessed or nearly flush; on the broad near photo wall four columns and six clear rows are visible above the landscape/base zone.

Silver facets carry strongly projecting rectangular window boxes with dark reveals and pale metallic sills. Their row positions and projection vary with the facet; avoid painting a continuous flush rectangular grid over the entire folded cluster.
Metal planes should read as pale brushed silver in diffuse light, with restrained panel seams. The official view does not support mirror-like chrome across every silver surface.
The two Vassar canopies differ: Gates has paired silver folded plates, while the far Dreyfoos canopy has a conspicuous blue edge/band. Preserve their separate locations.

Only one public frontage photograph has been visually inspected in this audit. Rear/Hockfield material regions and exact window-by-window placement are not verified; no rear facade or full 360-degree accuracy claim is supported.
